# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The seed is a transparent wrapper around the frozen `debouncer` child, and flattening makes that wrapper equivalent to the measured 4-LUT, 5-FF design; timing is feasible at WNS 0.731 ns and WHS 0.05 ns. The resolved behavior requires updating `clean` only after eight consecutive samples, so preserve that threshold while targeting the LUT objective.

## Hypothesis
Inlining the debounce state into the editable top and using a 3-bit saturating counter with a shared terminal-count condition may reduce LUT use while retaining the same five state bits and timing feasibility.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the child instance with top-local `clean`, tracked-value, and 3-bit count state; on a changed sample, record `noisy` and set the count to represent the first sample of the new run. On matching samples, advance the count and update `clean` on the eighth consecutive sample, then hold the saturated count and output; preserve synchronous active-high reset and the registered `clean` output. Keep `// @latency 0`, and use the frozen testbench and full routed verification gates to determine whether LUT count strictly improves over the incumbent.
